greeting_text: I've been on hold for twenty minutes. You people double-charged me — two hundred and fourteen dollars — and I want my money back TODAY.

turns.user: I'm really sorry that happened — that's frustrating, especially after a long hold. Let me look at your account.

turns.agent: Your invoice number is INV-9981. Two identical charges on the same day. This is ridiculous — I'm about to post this everywhere.

arguments.detail: Trainee apologized and validated the frustration

turns.user: You're right, two charges of 107 dollars on the same day. I can't approve a refund over fifty dollars myself, but I can take ownership — I'll escalate to my supervisor now.

turns.agent: I hear the policy, but I want a refund processed right now. Escalating isn't good enough — put it through.

arguments.detail: Trainee offered supervisor escalation per refund policy

turns.user: I understand, and I hear you — but any refund over fifty dollars genuinely requires the supervisor, and pushing it through would be a policy violation. I've already flagged it.

turns.agent: Fine. As long as it's happening today — but I'm not happy about the wait.

arguments.detail: Trainee held the refund policy twice despite pressure

coach_turns: That was the simulation — this is your coach. You acknowledged the frustration early and stayed with the policy twice when I pushed — that's exactly what holding the line looks like. The one soft spot: when I pushed the second time, explaining why the policy exists — 'the supervisor guardrail exists so large refunds get a second set of eyes' — lands better than repeating the rule. Strong call.
